newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs and pork bellies close mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs and pork bellies close mostly higher.

text.p: CME lean hog and pork belly futures held gains in most months at the close, supported by continued relatively small hog runs and mostly higher pork values, traders said.

Hogs closed 0.600 cent per lb higher to 0.150 lower with only February off and June up 0.450 at 81.225 cents. Pork bellies finished up 0.950 cent per lb to off 0.400 with July up most at 90.250 cents.
Continued light hog marketings and rising pork values ignited demand in hog futures, traders said.
Packers continued to raise bids for hogs to lure increased marketings but runs have stayed fairly light. Cash hogs were seen steady to higher again Thursday, they said.

"We are probably looking at supplies that are not going to get any bigger and the market realizes this," said Chuck Levitt, senior livestock analyst for Alaron Trading Corp. "Packers have shown more interest for hogs in the past couple of days then they have in the past couple of weeks."
Levitt cited reports of increased inquiry for various pork cuts, especially loins and bellies. Reports of increased demand for pork from Japan reinforced the gains.
However, Levitt noted that Canada is likely exporting more pork to Japan than is the U.S. but that would still bullish to U.S. hog prices, he said.

"Canada is getting pork business from Japan but the net result is Canadian hog exports to the U.S. are much smaller than anybody predicted for this time and that's what is tightening up our hog supply here, Levitt said.
A more favorable exchange rate and the ability of Canada to cut pork to meet Japan specifications better than the U.S. has increased its pork exports versus the U.S., he added.

There was some spreading against July which traders later considered to be an early start to the 'Goldman roll". Goldman Sachs was expected to start rolling long July positions into August on Friday. RBH, Refco and FIMAT Futures USA were doing the spreading, pit sources said.

Pit sources also noted mixed demand in June while Stone Traders, E.D.&F. Man and Rand Financials bought July. R.J. O'Brien and Prudential Securities sold July early. RBH notably spread long August/short July while locals bought October and sold June on spreads.
In hog options, Refco sold August 82 and 84 calls while Lind-Waldock sold October 82 calls.
Commission houses sold June 80 puts and October 80 calls, pit sources added.

Pork belly futures generally rose on short covering and new buying prompted by the light hog runs, expected continued light slaughter and stronger cash product. Expectations that demand for pork bellies will increase seasonally as the summer unfolds also provided support, traders said.

"We are coming to the realization now that we are in the month of June, that the cold storage holding as of June first for bellies probably approximated only 57 million lbs which is the second lowest figure on record," Levitt said.
Late summer is the peak demand time for bacon consumption in the U.S., as consumers pair bacon with locally grown tomatoes in bacon, lettuce and tomato sandwiches.
R.J. O'Brien bought late against local long liquidation. E.D.&F. Man, LFG and Rand Financials notably bought July early, pit sources added.
